newsitem.title: USA: California Senate panel OKs $69 bln budget plan.
newsitem.headline: California Senate panel OKs $69 bln budget plan.

text.p: The California Senate's Budget and Fiscal Review Committee on Tuesday approved a $69 billion spending plan for fiscal year 1997-1998, sending it to the full Senate for review.
The Democrat-controlled committee approved the budget plan on a vote of 10-to-0.
The full Senate is scheduled to take up the budget proposal on Thursday.
The Senate budget committee's spending plan is about $800 million larger than Republican Gov. Pete Wilson's latest budget proposal, the committee said.

The Senate committee proposes spending $600 million more on welfare reform than the governor. The committee's budget also includes a $325 million renters' tax credit and $250 million to give a pay raise to state employees.
The committee's budget does not include the 10 percent bank and corporation tax cut proposed by Wilson.
